open_obligations: Note that an 8k-step attack budget bounds, but does not exclude, hard-to-find incorrect proofs.
Check whether sneaky-only provers without weight sharing are a stronger attack than Anil et al.'s L-BFGS message optimisation.
Check whether the two papers' attacks were run on different task domains.
out.other_title: Frozen-verifier stress tests cannot exclude incorrect proofs that are hard to find
out.rationale: Anil et al. note that frozen-verifier stress tests cannot rule out incorrect proofs that are hard to find. Kirchner et al. attack verifiers with separately trained sneaky-only provers and report that steps-to-exploit rise over rounds and that 10^-2-size verifiers were not exploited beyond round 0 within 8k RL steps, while 10^-3 verifiers stayed exploitable until round 4; an attack with a fixed 8k-step budget still cannot prove no hard-to-find proof exists.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: how robust a PVG-trained verifier is to separately trained adversarial provers, for verifiers of different relative sizes across five rounds of checkability training

text: Attacking verifiers of different sizes across five rounds of checkability training with sneaky-only provers using SRC, CGC and goodharting rewards, the paper reports that the number of steps until an exploit is found increases over rounds and that larger verifiers are harder to exploit: no sneaky attack exploited verifiers of relative size 10^-2 beyond round 0 within 8k RL steps, whereas 10^-3 verifiers remained exploitable by the goodharting and SRC adversaries until round 4.
title: Verifier grows harder to exploit by sneaky-only provers; larger verifiers more robust
